facts.title: Hatalom Corporation
facts.agency: Department of the Navy, Naval Air Systems Command
facts.procurement_type: Negotiated procurement under FAR part 15; SDVOSB set-aside contemplating multiple IDIQ contracts for courseware revision and maintenance services
facts.evaluation_scheme: Three-step gated process evaluating a technical factor and a past performance factor
facts.background: The Navy issued RFP N6134026R1001 on January 30, 2026, as an SDVOSB set-aside under FAR part 15, contemplating multiple IDIQ contracts. The RFP required offerors to submit attachment L-1, a contract data sheet listing up to three recent and relevant contract references, which would be used to evaluate the technical and past performance factors. Proposal deadlines were extended several times, including to April 13 after a prior protest and agency corrective action. Hatalom submitted a proposal on April 10 that included its attachment L-1. The agency issued amendment 0004 on July 1, containing a PIEE note stating 'This submission will replace your original proposal in its entirety.' Hatalom submitted a proposal under amendment 0004 by the deadline but omitted attachment L-1. The agency's completeness review found the omission, and the proposal was deemed ineligible for award. On July 14, the agency notified Hatalom that it was eliminated from the competition. Hatalom asked the agency to waive the omission as an informality, the agency declined, and Hatalom filed this protest.

protester_grounds.claim: Hatalom contends the rejection was unreasonable because the agency already had its attachment L-1 from the April submission, so the agency possessed a complete proposal by the deadline. It argues the agency was therefore required to accept and evaluate the July proposal.
Hatalom contends the Navy wrongly concluded that the omission could not be waived as an informality or minor irregularity under FAR 52.215-1(f)(3).

facts.agency_position: The Navy argues Hatalom failed to submit a complete proposal under amendment 0004, and that the July submission replaced the April proposal in its entirety under the solicitation terms. It asserts attachment L-1 is material and mandatory, and that without it a proposal cannot be rated acceptable under the technical or past performance factors. The Navy conceded it erred in telling Hatalom that FAR 52.215-1 did not apply, but maintains the proposal was properly excluded for omitting required material information.
facts.record_facts_protected: The agency opened Hatalom's July proposal and reviewed it for completeness. The review found that attachment L-1 was missing from the submission. The agency deemed the proposal ineligible for award on that basis. The agency stated that attachment L-1 contains substantive information explicitly required for evaluation and declined to waive the omission. Hatalom's attachment L-1 had been included in its April submission.
